To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we show that risk minimization with the loss function based upon mean absolute value of the error is inherently robust under label noise for multilabel classification problems, (ii) we show that the widely used loss function based on the cross-entropy of the predicted probability and true label is not robust to label noise, and (iii) we provide some theoretical results on loss function that are inherently robust to label noises for multilabel problems.

(1) we provide sufficient conditions on a multiclass loss function so that it is robust to label noise, (2) these conditions generalize existing results for binary classification, and (3) we show that the mean absolute value of the error is a noise tolerant loss function.
(1) there are loss functions that are intrinsically noise robust, and (2) these loss functions are not the same for binary classification and multiclass classification.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for multiclass classification, risk minimization with mean absolute error loss function is inherently robust to noise and thus back propagation is enough for learning the true classifier under label noise.
for deep learning under label noise, we can use standard risk minimization with a loss function that is inherently tolerant to label error.
for deep learning, one should look for loss functions which are inherently noise tolerant and not modify the architecture of the network or use complex algorithms for estimating true label.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current techniques for handling label noise in learning deep networks can be simplified by replacing the existing loss functions with a loss function that is inherently robust to noisy labels.
for learning neural networks under label noise, one does not need to estimate the true labels.
there exist loss functions that are noise tolerant, and these can be used to train deep networks with label noise.
